# MCP tools

<!-- Generated by scripts/reference-docs.py from the isocast binary; do not edit. -->

`isocast mcp` serves Isocast to AI agents over MCP (stdin and stdout).
Each tool is a method of the same API the app and the CLI use. Add it to
a client, for example:

```sh
claude mcp add isocast -- isocast mcp
```

78 tools. Arguments marked required must be given; ids, not names,
address sources, scenes and clips. Errors name the field and list the
valid options.

## add_marker

Mark this moment in the recording with a label; it is written to the manifest with its time.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `label` (required) | string | What happens at this moment, like "intro" or "retake". |

## add_plugin

Install a plugin from a local folder with an isocast-plugin.toml (path: absolute). `grant` must be exactly the permissions its manifest asks for: without it nothing is installed and the error lists them, so the user can see them before you grant them. A newer version replaces the installed one (needing a grant only if it asks for more); force reinstalls the same or an older version; link runs it from the folder instead of a copy. Its process, if any, starts at once, sandboxed, and may call only the methods it was granted.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `force` | boolean | Install it even if the same or a newer version is installed. |
| `grant` | Permissions | The permissions granted, which must be exactly what the manifest asks for. Without it nothing is installed, and the error lists what the plugin asks for. An upgrade that asks for no more than was granted before needs none. |
| `link` | boolean | Keep a link to the folder instead of copying it (for developing a plugin): it is read again each time the plugin starts. |
| `path` (required) | string | The plugin's folder (with its isocast-plugin.toml), as an absolute path. |

## apply_change

Make a change to the live setup, atomically, if it is still at `revision` and the result has no problems. It takes effect at once, in a recording or stream too, except that sources being recorded keep their devices until the recording stops and the canvas can't change while recording or streaming.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `live` | boolean | One step of a gesture (many changes a second, e.g. moving a source smoothly): applied at once and saved to disk a moment after the last step instead of before replying. |
| `patch` | any | Or a JSON merge patch on the live setup. Lists of items with ids (sources and scenes by "id", scene items by "id" or else "source") merge by id: {"sources":[{"id":"facecam","device":"Capture Card"}]} changes one field, {"sources":[{"id":"iphone","remove":true}]} removes a source. |
| `revision` (required) | integer | The revision from plan_change or get_setup (0 when there is no live setup yet). The change is refused if the live setup has moved on. |
| `setup` | object (optional) | A whole new setup to replace the live one (the shape get_setup returns; get_setup_schema has its JSON Schema). |

## bug_report

Generate a sanitized offline bug-report zip or preview every included file. Includes environment, logs, metrics, crashes and manifests, never media. Nothing is uploaded unless submit is true: then ISSUE.md becomes a public GitHub issue and the zip is kept privately for maintainers (pass preview_id to send exactly a reviewed preview). Only submit when the user asked to send the report; on failure the zip is kept and submit_error says why.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `describe` | string (optional) |  |
| `hash_paths` | boolean | Strict privacy: per-report HMAC pseudonyms for paths, titles and device identities. |
| `launches` | integer (optional) | Last launches of each process to collect (1..10; default 3). |
| `out` | string (optional) | Absolute or ~/ output directory; defaults to Downloads/Isocast Reports (isolated engines: beside their logs). |
| `preview` | boolean | Return the file index, ISSUE and redaction report without writing a zip. Use report_file with the returned preview_id to page through contents. |
| `preview_id` | string (optional) | With `submit`: send exactly this preview (from an earlier `preview`) instead of collecting again. |
| `submit` | boolean | Also send the report: the zip is written, then its ISSUE.md becomes a public GitHub issue and the zip is kept privately for maintainers. Never implied; if sending fails the zip is kept and `submit_error` says why. |

## check_setup

Check this Mac against a setup (the live setup if none is given): permissions, hardware encoders, whether each source's device is connected and what format it would record, and the recording disk's free space and speed. Each check has a status and, if needed, a fix.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string (optional) | Check this folder instead of the setup's recording.folder. |
| `setup` | object (optional) | The setup to check; the live setup if absent (the shape get_setup returns; get_setup_schema has its JSON Schema). |

## clear_preview

Leave Studio Mode by clearing its staged preview. Program stays on air.

## clear_stream_key

Remove the stored stream key for a streaming service (the live setup's by default).

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `server` | string (optional) | For "custom": the server the key belongs to. |
| `service` | StreamService | The service; the live setup's [stream] service if absent. |

## close_timeline

Make no timeline current: takes are only recorded, as without timelines. Returns the id of the timeline that was current.

## create_collection_or_profile

Make a scene collection (one empty scene on the canvas in use) or a profile (60 fps, HEVC program and ISO files to ~/Movies/Isocast), or a copy of one (copy_of: its id, OBS's Duplicate); with switch, start using it.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `copy_of` | string (optional) | Copy this one (by id) instead of starting blank (OBS's Duplicate). A blank collection has one empty scene on the current canvas; a blank profile records 60 fps HEVC with ISO files to ~/Movies/Isocast. |
| `id` | string (optional) | Its id (lowercase letters, digits and dashes); made from the name if absent. |
| `kind` (required) | LibraryKind |  |
| `name` (required) | string | Its name. |
| `switch` | boolean | Switch to it once made (refused while recording or streaming). |

## delete_collection_or_profile

Delete a scene collection or profile that isn't in use (switch away first); its file is kept in the library's deleted folder.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | string |  |
| `kind` (required) | LibraryKind |  |

## developer_mode

Developer mode, for testing a build locally. With no arguments, read it: whether the current profile has it on, whether isocastd is writing its verbose records and traces, when it turns itself off, its logs folder and budget, and the latest per-second trace (each recording output's frames, drops, late frames, encode submit and capture-to-submit times, writer queue; compositor and pacing). With `enabled` (and/or `auto_off_hours`, 0 for never; 24 by default), change it: every API call and debug messages are logged and frame timing traced while recording, in their own log segments (read them with get_logs). Never disturbs a running recording.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `auto_off_hours` | integer (optional) | Hours until it turns itself off (0: never). |
| `enabled` | boolean (optional) |  |

## discover_obs

Find OBS Studio's scene collections and profiles on this Mac (its settings folder, or `folder`) without importing anything: each collection with scene and source counts and the profile an import would use (`profile`, a basic.ini path), each profile's canvas, frame rate, recording encoder, format and folder, and stream service and bitrate (never the key; `key_in_file` says OBS keeps one in plain text), and files that couldn't be read. Offer the collections to the user, then import_obs_collection_or_profile with the collection's `file` and its `profile` (stream_key only if the user agreed to move the key).

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string (optional) | Look in this folder instead of OBS's (`~/Library/Application Support/obs-studio`, or the daemon's `$ISOCAST_OBS_FOLDER`). |

## estimate_capacity

Predict instantly, without benchmarking, whether a setup's files (the live setup's if none is given) fit this Mac's H.264/HEVC media engines, from measured per-chip data: `capacity` is fits, no_margin or cannot_keep_up, `load` the busiest engine's share, and `suggestions` the closest changes that fit (each a patch for plan_change, or a method like stream_stop; `after_take` ones wait for the recording to end). With add_iso, `admission` says how to turn that ISO file on so it fits (smaller, slower, or left off). tune_encoders measures instead.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `add_iso` | string (optional) | A video source id whose ISO file would be turned on: `admission` says how to add it so the setup still fits, and why. |
| `setup` | object (optional) | The setup to judge; the live setup (at its sources' live formats) if absent (the shape get_setup returns). |
| `stream` | boolean (optional) | Count the stream's encode. Default: the live setup's if it streams now; a given setup's if it has a stream. |

## export_timeline

Join a timeline's clips (the current one unless `timeline` is given), in order, into one program file and one file per ISO source every clip has (video copied as recorded, audio re-encoded once so it stays in sync at every join), plus an .export.json manifest, next to the first take (or in `folder`). Sources some clips lack are skipped, saying why. It runs in the background: returns at once with the files it will write; get_events shows export_progress and export_finished.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string (optional) | Where to write the joined files (made if missing); else the folder of the first clip's take. |
| `timeline` | string (optional) | The timeline's id; the current one if absent. |

## get_collection_or_profile

One scene collection or profile (kind: collection or profile, and its id) as a document, to export it or read one that isn't in use.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | string |  |
| `kind` (required) | LibraryKind |  |

## get_data

Read the data store: values by key (dotted ids like score.home) that text in scenes shows (a text source's or text content's `data = "score.home"`). Every key, the `keys` given, or those under `prefix` (`score` covers score and score.home); with the store's revision, which keys are kept across restarts (persisted), and asked keys that aren't set (missing).

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `keys` | list of string | The keys to read; every key if neither this nor `prefix` is given. |
| `prefix` | string (optional) | Or the keys under this prefix: `score` reads `score` and `score.home`, not `scoreboard`. |

## get_events

What happened since you last looked: warnings (like a file dropping frames), recordings starting and stopping (with the report), scene switches, markers, stream and source state, the newest setup_changed and live status, and `connection` events when isocastd goes away or comes back. The server keeps the newest 500 whether or not anyone reads. Pass the reply's `next` as `after` to get only newer events; `kinds` filters, `wait_seconds` waits for one to arrive.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `after` | integer (optional) | Only events after this one: the `next` of the previous read. Without it, the newest events. |
| `kinds` | array (optional) | Only these kinds, like ["warning","stopped"]. All kept kinds if absent. |
| `limit` | integer (optional) | The most events to return (1 to 500, default 50). |
| `wait_seconds` | number (optional) | If no event matches yet, wait up to this many seconds (at most 30) for one. |

## get_logs

Read structured engine/client logs with severity/component filters and a cursor for subsequent reads.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `component` | string (optional) | Component substring. |
| `cursor` | object (optional) | Opaque per-file byte offsets returned by the previous call. |
| `level` | string (optional) | Minimum severity: debug, info, warn, error. |
| `limit` | integer (optional) | Maximum returned records (1..1000; default 200). |

## get_permissions

The screen recording, camera and microphone permissions, without asking, with the next step for each that isn't granted: request it, or turn it on in System Settings (which app, which pane, and whether isocastd must restart afterwards).

## get_setup

The live setup document (sources, scenes, recording settings) and its revision, with the scene collection and profile it is kept in. Revision 0 means no setup has been applied yet. With resolved: true, also where every item is drawn as laid out (items with a `layout`): each item's rect in its parent, its box on the canvas and its transform, with the layout's generation (frames carry the one they show).

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `resolved` | boolean | Also return where every item is drawn, as laid out (`resolved`). |

## get_setup_schema

The JSON Schema of a setup document (what get_setup returns and plan_change, apply_change, start_recording and check_setup take): every source kind, scene item field, filter, transition and recording setting, with descriptions. Large; read it before writing a setup or a patch by hand.

## get_status

Whether Isocast is idle or recording, with live frame and drop counters, the files being written, the scene on air, the last session's report, the stream (state, bitrates, dropped frames, congestion, reconnects, whether a key is set), the live engine's frame rate (engine.fps of canvas.fps), each live source's size and frame rate (engine.sources: fps opened at, received_fps measured), isocastd's CPU use (cpu_percent, of all cores), the recording disk's free space (recording_free_bytes) and how fast the program file fills it at most (program_bytes_per_second), and which isocastd answered (daemon: version, build, commit, executable, pid; an engine left running from before an app update reports the old build).

## get_timeline

A timeline (the current one unless `timeline` gives an id): its clips in order, each with its id (c1, c2…), place and length on the timeline, take (session manifest), status and files (program and ISO files), and the takes taken off it (their files are kept where they are).

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `timeline` | string (optional) | A timeline's id (`timeline_list` has them); the current one if absent. |

## hotkeys_actions

List bindable action ids, labels, groups, strict argument schemas, reserved actions, key names and opt-in defaults.

## hotkeys_get

Get current profile hotkeys, global registration warnings, held audio overrides and Studio Mode state.

## hotkeys_input

Forward focused key input: keys and phase (press or release), including globally registered chords. Matching native and focused press edges within 100 ms fire once. Send releases on blur; persistent clients use the same socket for both edges.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `keys` (required) | string |  |
| `phase` (required) | Phase |  |

## hotkeys_set

Replace all profile bindings with bindings, or patch by binding id (null removes). Keys use ctrl+alt+shift+cmd+key syntax. hotkeys_actions lists typed arguments, key names and defaults. Invalid/conflicting chords change nothing.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bindings` | object (optional) | Replace all bindings, including an empty map to disable them all. |
| `patch` | object (optional) | Or replace bindings by id; null removes one. Exactly one of bindings/patch. |
| `revision` | integer (optional) | Optional optimistic concurrency check, from hotkeys_get. |

## import_collection_or_profile

Add a scene collection and/or profile from documents (as get_collection_or_profile returns them), or both from a whole setup. Refused if one has problems of its own; problems with the other half in use are reported. With switch, start using them.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `collection` | object (optional) | Or a scene collection, as get_collection_or_profile returns one: the setup's version, name, canvas.width/height, sources, scenes, transition and recording.program.audio / recording.iso.sources / recording.iso.audio. |
| `name` | string (optional) | The name to give them; their own if absent. |
| `profile` | object (optional) | And/or a profile: version, name, canvas.fps, audio, stream and the rest of recording (folder, keep_free_gb, program and iso settings). |
| `setup` | object (optional) | A whole setup (as get_setup returns one): its collection part and its profile part are both imported. |
| `switch` | boolean | Switch to what was imported (refused while recording or streaming). |

## import_obs_collection

Read an OBS Studio scene collection into an Isocast setup: sources (ids made from their names), scenes and items, filters and the transition, devices matched against this Mac. Returns the setup, what couldn't come over and why, notes to check, and counts. Doesn't change the live setup: pass the setup to plan_change and apply_change.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `collection` (required) | string | The collection: an absolute path to its .json file, or its name in OBS's scenes folder, like "Recording". |
| `fps` | integer (optional) | The canvas frame rate; the profile's if absent. |
| `height` | integer (optional) |  |
| `profile` | string (optional) | The OBS profile with the frame rate and recording settings (a name or a basic.ini path); found automatically if absent. |
| `width` | integer (optional) | Import onto a canvas this wide and high, scaling positions and sizes; the collection's own canvas if absent. |

## import_obs_collection_or_profile

Add an OBS Studio scene collection (its name in OBS's scenes folder, or an absolute .json path) as a scene collection, and/or an OBS profile (its name, folder or basic.ini) as a profile, with devices matched against this Mac. Returns what was made and what couldn't come over. Give both to bring Source Record's ISO settings into the profile.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `collection` | string (optional) | An OBS scene collection: its .json file (absolute or `~/...`), or its name in OBS's scenes folder, like "Recording". |
| `height` | integer (optional) |  |
| `name` | string (optional) | The name to give them; OBS's if absent. |
| `profile` | string (optional) | An OBS profile: its name, its folder or its basic.ini path. |
| `stream_key` | boolean | Move the stream key OBS keeps in plain text in the profile's service.json into the Keychain, for the imported profile's service (only when the user agreed to it). Without it the key stays behind. |
| `switch` | boolean | Switch to what was imported (refused while recording or streaming). |
| `width` | integer (optional) | Import the collection onto a canvas this wide and high, scaling positions and sizes about the centre; its own canvas if absent. |

## init_setup

Make a good starting setup from this Mac's devices: the main display, the best real camera (USB, then Continuity, then built-in; virtual cameras only if nothing else), the default microphone and desktop audio, in scenes screen-and-camera (camera as a corner picture-in-picture), camera and screen, recording the 1080p60 program plus ISO files of the screen and camera to ~/Movies/Isocast. Every choice can be overridden. Devices without permission become placeholders, and the notes say what to do. With apply, it becomes the live setup.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `apply` | boolean | Make it the live setup, replacing any (the old one stays in the setup file's .bak). Otherwise it is only returned, for plan_change. |
| `camera` | string (optional) | The camera: an id, a name or part of one from `isocast devices`, or "none". If absent, the best real camera: a USB or other external camera, else Continuity Camera, else the built-in one; virtual cameras (OBS, NDI) and Desk View only if there is nothing else. |
| `display` | string (optional) | The display to capture: "main", or an id or name from `isocast devices`. The main display if absent. |
| `folder` | string (optional) | Where recordings go; `~/Movies/Isocast` if absent. |
| `fps` | integer (optional) | Canvas frame rate: 60 if absent (or the display's, if it refreshes more slowly). |
| `height` | integer (optional) |  |
| `layout` | Layout | Where the camera goes in the "Screen + Camera" scene. |
| `microphone` | string (optional) | The microphone: "default" (the system's default input, if absent), an id, a name or part of one, or "none". |
| `name` | string (optional) | The setup's name; "My setup" if absent. |
| `system_audio` | boolean (optional) | Put what this Mac plays (system audio) in the program; yes if absent. |
| `width` | integer (optional) | The canvas, 1920×1080 if absent. |

## list_collections_and_profiles

The scene collections (scenes, sources, transitions and the canvas size) and profiles (frame rate, recording, stream and audio settings) the live setup can be made of, as in OBS, and which of each is in use (`collection`, `profile`). The live setup is the pair in use: apply_change edits it, and the change is saved into the right one.

## list_devices

Displays, windows, cameras (capture cards, Continuity Camera, iPhone screens over USB), microphones with their ids and formats, audio outputs (for audio.monitoring_device), and the screen/camera/microphone permissions.

## list_encoder_options

List recording encoders with their display labels and supported containers. Use this before changing program or ISO encoder settings.

## list_plugins

The installed plugins: id, version, what they provide (a process, and kinds like twitch-chat/glow), state (ok, disabled, incompatible or failed, and why), their process (running or restarting, restarts, how it last ended, its log) and the permissions they were granted.

## list_projects

The recording projects, newest first: each recording session writes into its own folder (`<date> <time> Untitled` in the recordings folder) with every take's program and ISO files, manifests and exports. Each has an id (stable across renames), name, folder, takes (manifests) and files. Optional `limit` (100 if absent).

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer (optional) | At most this many, newest first: 100 if absent. |

## list_timelines

Every timeline (id, name, clips, length) and which is current (the one finished takes are added to).

## live_engine

Keep the live engine running (running: true), as OBS does, so the live setup's sources, program and mix run all the time and recording starts at once; or let it stop once nothing needs it (running: false). Returns {engine}: the engine's sources and how each is doing, or null once stopped.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `running` (required) | boolean | true keeps the live engine running; false lets it stop once nothing (a recording, a stream, a client showing frames) needs it. |

## live_frame

See the live engine's newest frame as a JPEG: the program (exactly what records and streams), studio mode's preview scene, or a running video source. Starts the live engine if it isn't running, which opens the live setup's devices.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `target` | string (optional) | "program" (the default), "preview" (studio mode's preview scene) or a video source id of the live setup. |
| `width` | integer (optional) | Scale the picture down to at most this many pixels wide (default 1280). |

## move_clip

Move a clip (by id) to another place on a timeline: `index` counts from 0 (the first). Returns the timeline.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `clip` (required) | string | The clip's id, like `c3`. |
| `index` (required) | integer | Where it goes, counting from 0 (the first clip) to the number of clips less one (the last). |
| `timeline` | string (optional) | The timeline's id; the current one if absent. |

## new_timeline

Make a timeline (optional `name`) and make it current: from now on every take that finishes (stop_recording, or split_take) is added to its end as a clip. A timeline is takes in order, like a clip bar: retake records the last one again, remove_clip and move_clip edit the order, and export_timeline joins them into one file. Returns the timeline.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string (optional) | Its name; "Timeline N" if absent. Its id is made from it. |

## open_permission_settings

Open System Settings on the user's screen at the pane where a permission (screen_recording, camera or microphone) is turned on by hand, for one that was refused.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `permission` (required) | PermissionKind | screen_recording, camera or microphone. |

## open_timeline

Make a timeline current (by id), so finished takes are added to it.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `timeline` (required) | string | The id of the timeline to make current. |

## optimize_setup

Optimize the live setup for `goal` recording, streaming or both (OBS's Auto-Configuration Wizard). Recording favours quality and ISO files (HEVC High, an ISO file per captured source); streaming sets the service and a bitrate from the upload speed (upload_kbps, or measured like test_upload_speed; never for a custom server, test it first) and sizes the stream to it. Then it benchmarks this Mac like tune_encoders and steps down where it can't keep up. Returns a one-line `summary`, the optimized setup, its differences from the live setup, the benchmark and notes; with apply it becomes the live setup. Takes a minute or two; refused while recording or streaming.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `apply` | boolean | Make the result the live setup (refused while recording or streaming). |
| `folder` | string (optional) | Benchmark writing to this folder instead of the setup's `recording.folder`. |
| `goal` (required) | Goal |  |
| `server` | string (optional) | Streaming: its ingest server, if not the service's default (needed for custom and Kick). |
| `service` | StreamService | Streaming: the service; the live setup's stream service if absent. |
| `upload_kbps` | integer (optional) | Streaming: the upload speed in kb/s (from `speed_test`, or known); measured with `speed_test` if absent. |

## pause_recording

Pause the same recording files on a shared video/audio boundary. Streaming continues. Markers land at the paused playhead; resume before split or retake.

## plan_change

Work out what a change to the live setup would do, without making it: the differences (paths use ids) and any problems. Give either a whole setup or a patch.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `patch` | any | Or a JSON merge patch on the live setup. Lists of items with ids (sources and scenes by "id", scene items by "id" or else "source") merge by id: {"sources":[{"id":"facecam","device":"Capture Card"}]} changes one field, {"sources":[{"id":"iphone","remove":true}]} removes a source. |
| `setup` | object (optional) | A whole new setup to replace the live one (the shape get_setup returns; get_setup_schema has its JSON Schema). |

## preview_frame

See what is happening, as a PNG image: the program by default (while recording, exactly the frame it recorded last), the preview scene, a scene by id, a source of the live setup (of the recording, while recording), or a quick source like "screen" or "camera:NAME".

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `preview` | boolean | Or, with neither, the scene in preview. |
| `scene` | string (optional) | Or a scene id. With neither, the program (while recording, exactly the frame it recorded last). |
| `source` | string (optional) | A source id in the live setup, or a quick source like "screen", "display:NAME", "camera:NAME" or "test-pattern". |
| `width` | integer (optional) | Scale the picture down to at most this many pixels wide (default 1280). |

## preview_scene

Stage a scene in preview, by id, without changing what is on air; take_preview then puts it on air.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `scene` (required) | string | The id of a scene in the setup. |

## read_bug_report_file

Read a UTF-8 page (default 4096 bytes, max 16384) from a redacted bug-report preview. Use its preview_id and a file-index name; next_offset continues. Preview expires after five idle minutes.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `file` (required) | string |  |
| `limit` | integer (optional) | UTF-8 bytes, 1..16384; default 4096. Responses end at a character boundary. |
| `offset` | integer |  |
| `preview_id` (required) | string |  |

## refresh_browser

Reload a browser source's page in the running recording, bypassing the cache, for example after changing the page or when it stopped updating.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `source` (required) | string | The browser source's id. |

## remove_clip

Take a clip (by id, like c2) off a timeline (the current one unless `timeline` is given). Only the timeline changes: the take's files stay where they were recorded, listed under the timeline's `removed`. Returns the timeline.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `clip` (required) | string | The clip's id, like `c2`. |
| `timeline` | string (optional) | The timeline's id; the current one if absent. |

## remove_plugin

Stop a plugin's process and remove the plugin (by id); its data folder is kept if it wrote anything there. Refused while the live setup uses its kinds (the error lists where) unless `force`: the setup then keeps them, bypassed, until the plugin is added again.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `force` | boolean | Remove it even though the live setup uses its kinds: the setup keeps them as they are, bypassed (a filter's sound passes through), until the plugin is added again. |
| `id` (required) | string | The plugin's id. |

## rename_collection_or_profile

Rename a scene collection or profile; its id stays. Renaming the collection in use renames the live setup.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | string |  |
| `kind` (required) | LibraryKind |  |
| `name` (required) | string |  |

## rename_project

Rename a recording project (by id, from list_projects): its folder becomes `<date> <time> <name>` (numbered if taken). Refused while a recording or an export writes into it. Manifests and timelines keep finding its files. Returns the project, its old name and old folder.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | string | Its new name: the folder becomes `<date> <time> <name>`. |
| `project` (required) | string | The project's id (from `list_projects` or a `project_created` event). |

## replay_status

The replay buffer's state, seconds held, memory used and its limit, format, whether it shares the stream's encoder, missed frames and the last save.

## request_permissions

Ask macOS for screen recording, camera and microphone access where it hasn't been decided yet (or only `permission`). Its prompts appear on the user's screen; waits up to a minute for answers and returns the permissions with next steps.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `permission` | PermissionKind | Only this one: screen_recording, camera or microphone (all three not decided yet if left out). |

## restart_isocastd

Restart isocastd, which only sees a permission granted in System Settings (screen recording, above all) once restarted; the live setup is kept. Refused, atomically by isocastd, while it records, streams, exports or feeds the virtual camera.

## resume_recording

Resume a paused recording into its existing files. Paused time is cut out of the files and recorded in the manifest.

## retake

Record the last take again, on the current timeline. Not recording: take the last clip off (its files stay) and start recording in the same folder (or `folder`; `seconds` stops it on its own); while a stop is finishing, the same once it has. Recording: drop the take being recorded from the timeline (its files stay) and begin a new take about a quarter second later without stopping any device; `begins_at` and `begins_in_seconds` say when (what is said before then is in the dropped take). Returns the new take's files and what was taken off. Program export needs every clip's program file.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string (optional) | Write the new take here; else the folder of the take it replaces (else the setup's `recording.folder`). Not while recording, where the new take goes where the recording writes. |
| `seconds` | number (optional) | Stop on its own after this many seconds (not while recording). |

## save_replay

Save the replay buffer: write the last recording.replay.seconds of the program, up to this moment, to a new MOV/MP4 in the recordings folder (the running recording's project folder, if one records), without interrupting recording or streaming. Returns the file's path, length, frames and any missed frames.

## set_audio

Change an audio source's program mix in the live setup: gain, mute, sync offset, balance and monitoring (hearing it through the setup's audio.monitoring_device). A running recording follows all but the offset at once. Each source's level, and the monitor's, is in get_status while recording.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `balance` | number (optional) | Where it sits between left (-1) and right (1) in the program mix; 0 is the centre. |
| `gain_db` | number (optional) | Volume change in the program mix, in dB (-60 to 24; 0 is as captured). |
| `monitor` | Monitoring | Hear it through the setup's monitoring device: "monitor_only" (heard, but left out of the program mix), "monitor_and_output", or "off". |
| `mono` | boolean (optional) | Downmix stereo to mono before balance in the program and monitoring. |
| `muted` | boolean (optional) | Leave it out of the program mix (true) or put it back (false). |
| `offset_ms` | integer (optional) | Shift its audio later (positive) or earlier, in ms, in every file; applies from the next recording. |
| `source` (required) | string | The id of an audio source in the live setup. |

## set_data

Set data keys to JSON values, several at once (all of them, or none if one is refused): `values` like {"title": "Hello", "score.home": 3}. Text showing a key (`data = "title"` on a text source or text content) changes in the program within a frame or two, with no setup change, so use this for anything that changes while recording: titles, scores, counters. Keys: lowercase letters, digits, dashes and underscores between dots, at most 128 characters; values at most 64 KB as JSON. `persist: true` keeps them with the scene collection across restarts (false stops keeping them; absent leaves that as it was). Returns the revision and the keys that changed.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `persist` | boolean (optional) | Keep these keys with the scene collection, so they come back after a restart (`true`), or stop keeping them (`false`). If absent, a key keeps what it had; a new key isn't kept. |
| `values` (required) | object | Keys and their new values (any JSON), set together: all of them or, if one is refused, none. |

## set_stream_key

Keep a stream key in the macOS Keychain for a streaming service (the live setup's by default). It is never written to setups, logs or status. Returns where it is kept, not the key.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `key` (required) | string | The stream key from the service's dashboard. It goes into the Keychain and is never shown again; prefer `isocast stream key set` in a terminal, which keeps it out of this conversation. |
| `server` | string (optional) | For "custom": the server it belongs to (rtmp://host/app). |
| `service` | StreamService | The service it is for; the live setup's [stream] service if absent. |

## split_take

Split the recording into a new take at the next whole second without stopping any device: the current files end there and new files, with their own manifest, begin. Returns the new take's files.

## start_recording

Start recording the live setup (or the given setup, which then replaces the live setup): the program and every ISO source, each to its own file. Returns once every file is created.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string (optional) | Absolute folder for the files instead of the setup's recording.folder. |
| `seconds` | number (optional) | Stop on its own after this many seconds. |
| `setup` | object (optional) | The setup to record; the live setup if absent (the shape get_setup returns; get_setup_schema has its JSON Schema). |

## start_replay

Start the replay buffer: keep the last recording.replay.seconds (30 by default) of the encoded program, video and program mix, in memory, starting the live engine if needed; recording and streaming are independent of it. It shares the stream's encoder when the setup has a [stream]. Then save_replay writes the last seconds to a file. Returns its status.

## start_stream

Go live: stream the program (canvas and program mix) as H.264/AAC over RTMP or RTMPS to the live setup's [stream] service (twitch, youtube, kick, facebook or a custom server), starting the live engine if needed; recordings start and stop independently. Needs a stream key set. Returns the stream's status once live, or an error saying what to do. get_status shows the stream's health.

## stop_recording

Stop recording and finish every file. Returns the report: each file, its frames, dropped frames, audio dropouts and the manifest path.

## stop_replay

Stop the replay buffer, discarding what it holds (save_replay first to keep it). Returns its final status.

## stop_stream

Stop streaming. Returns the stream's final status: frames sent and dropped, reconnects and the last error.

## switch_collection_or_profile

Start using another scene collection, profile or both (by id): the live setup becomes that pair at once and the live engine follows (a new collection goes on air from its first scene). Refused while recording or streaming, and when the pair would have problems (each named by field and part).

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `collection` | string (optional) | The scene collection to use, by id. |
| `profile` | string (optional) | The profile to use, by id. |

## switch_scene

Put a scene on air, by id, with a transition: cut, fade, swipe, slide, fade_to_color, luma_wipe, stinger or move (the scene's transition, else the setup's, by default). While recording, the switch is written to the manifest's scene timeline.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `scene` (required) | string | The id of a scene in the setup. |
| `transition` | Transition | How it comes on air, like {"kind":"fade","duration_ms":500}, {"kind":"swipe","direction":"up"} or {"kind":"cut"}; the scene's transition (else the setup's) if absent. |

## take_preview

Put the preview scene on air with a transition (the scene's, else the setup's, by default); the scene that was on air moves to preview.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `transition` | Transition | How the preview scene comes on air; its transition (else the setup's) if absent. |

## test_upload_speed

Measure the upload speed to a streaming service's ingest (the live setup's unless `service`/`server` say) with a few seconds of filler video: Twitch's bandwidth test mode (never on air) or a custom server (a relay would put the filler on air for a few seconds: ask the user first), using the stored stream key. YouTube, Facebook and Kick have no test mode, and without a key nothing can be tested: then `measured` is false, `reason` says why, and `recommended_kbps` is a safe default. Refused while streaming.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `seconds` | integer (optional) | How long to send for, 3 to 20 seconds; 8 if absent. |
| `server` | string (optional) | Its ingest server (`rtmp://host/app`); the service's default, or the live setup's, if absent. Required for custom and Kick. |
| `service` | StreamService | The service to test against; the live setup's stream service if absent. |

## tune_encoders

Benchmark the hardware encoders on a setup's video files (the live setup if none is given), all at once as in a recording, and say whether this Mac keeps up: `capacity` is fits, no_margin (keeps up, nothing to spare) or cannot_keep_up (frames will drop). If it doesn't fit, it benchmarks changes closest first (a smaller program file, a lower quality preset, half the frame rate, one ISO file fewer) and recommends the closest that fits as `change`, a patch for plan_change. start_recording warns when a setup exceeds what this measured. Takes up to a minute or two; refused while recording.

| Argument | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string (optional) | Check this folder instead of the setup's recording.folder. |
| `setup` | object (optional) | The setup to check; the live setup if absent (the shape get_setup returns; get_setup_schema has its JSON Schema). |

## virtual_camera_start

Start Isocast Virtual Camera. Takes no arguments: configure virtual_camera.target/scene/source/width/height through plan_change and apply_change first. Requires its signed/approved extension; never installs it. Recording and streaming stay independent.

## virtual_camera_status

Read virtual camera state, output format, sent/dropped frame counts, enqueue latency and last error. diagnostic-iosurface means a development probe, not an installed camera.

## virtual_camera_stop

Stop feeding Isocast Virtual Camera. Other applications see the extension's Isocast waiting card.
